brief: BlackRock upgrades U.S. Treasuries, moving short-term Treasuries to overweight and long-term Treasuries to neutral, after the 10-year yield rose 110bp this year to around 5.25%, hitting 24-year highs before retreating on strong auctions. The rise is driven mainly by higher real rates, not inflation expectations or term premium. Intensifying competition for capital is pushing up the neutral rate, while Middle East tensions and higher oil prices reversed Fed rate expectations, with markets pricing 160bp of additional tightening since January that BlackRock views as overdone. With term premium near 75bp, BlackRock estimates a 75bp cushion against further yield increases over 12 months before total returns turn negative, favoring the short end where it sees the greatest scope for tightening expectations to unwind. The upgrade is funded by downgrading U.S. equities to neutral, a short-term risk-management move around AI-buildout volatility rather than a change in AI conviction, and by trimming the JGB underweight and moving U.S. agency MBS to neutral. BlackRock keeps its EM equities overweight and flags September CPI and PPI this week as the next test for Fed expectations and Treasury yields.
